#### seam
*Variants:* seam links; strip seams; site seams, link seams (source).
- **Meaning.** A reflection hyperplane of the chessboard tiling: for the tiling of 1:284–289, the hyperplanes `x_a ∈ ℓℤ` through lattice sites ("the planes at multiples of `ℓ`"). The cells are the sets of sites lying strictly between consecutive seams. "Seam links" are the links with at least one endpoint on a seam; an observable that depends only on links with both endpoints in the open cell "reads no seam links" (1:286–287), and this is the support condition under which reflection positivity (Proposition ch01:lattice-rp) applies. "Strip seams" (1:316–317) are the two reflection planes bounding a strip of the one-coordinate chessboard argument. Not defined in v3.
  *Basis:* R (1:284–289, 316–317) for the planes; S for the two kinds and for the precise set of seam links. *Where:* 1:284, 287, 316, 323. *Proposed:* *reflection planes of the tiling*; *links meeting a reflection plane*.
  *Source:* Martin `existence/centered-estimates.tex:32–37`: "All seams have the same kind: put `δ = 1` for link seams and `δ = 0` for site seams. … Its strict chamber consists of the sites whose relative coordinates `r_i` satisfy `0 ≤ r_i < ℓ` for link seams, and `0 < r_i < ℓ` for site seams. Observables are complex, bounded, measurable and gauge invariant, and depend only on links with both endpoints in the indicated strict chamber"; `:56–60`: the reflection at the seam `(p,a)` is `x_a ↦ 2(b_a + ℓ p_a) − δ − x_a`; `:125–126` "no link crossing a seam is introduced". The two kinds are the site and link reflections of 1:242–247; the tiling of 1:284–289 has site seams.
*Across chapters:* chapter 1 only. At 1:322–323 ("explicit control of support, seams and divisibility") the three conditions are: support of each observable in the open cell, the kind and position of the reflection planes, and divisibility of the side of the torus by twice the cell length.
*See also:* slot; strip; placement (sense 2).

#### second cluster expansion
- **Meaning.** The expansion of the logarithm of chapter 8, applied after the "first expansion" (expand `e^V = 1 + (e^V − 1)` and take connected components of intersecting dependence regions, 9:81–89).
  *Basis:* R (9:81–89). *Where:* 9:44, 88–89, 148, 173, 192. *Proposed:* *exponentiation* (the *exponentiated cluster expansion*), the first operation being the *Mayer expansion*.
*Literature:* **exponentiated cluster expansion**; **exponentiation** (B88a p. 1; B88b p. 277: "the exponentiated cluster expansion of Sect. 7 [I]" ([I] is B87); B89b p. 390: "The exponentiation (1.98) completes the R-operation"); **cluster expansion** for the whole of Mayer step plus logarithm, for an ultralocal measure, and "cluster expansion with holes" when large-field regions are present (D1 p. 1330010-38, Lemma 21; App. B, p. 1330010-48: "We present an ultralocal version"; D2 p. 092301-83). The same object (the logarithm of the polymer sum). "Second" is v3's own. Adopted: *exponentiation* (*exponentiated cluster expansion*), after B89b p. 387: "The next step is a construction of an exponentiated cluster expansion … The first operation is the Mayer expansion of the exponential" (read by the coordinating agent).
*Across chapters:* chapter 9 only.
*See also:* first expansion.

#### section
*Variants:* local polynomial section; degree-`d` section; finite-section constants; section constant `C^sec`; global section; physical section `P_d^loc`; microscopic sections; normalized microscopic section.
- **Meaning.** A right inverse of the Taylor map: "A local polynomial section is a complex-linear map `P_d^loc : V_d →` {polynomial functions of finitely many link entries and their conjugates} with `Tay_d P_d^loc[c] = c` … The term section simply means a right inverse of the Taylor map." Hence the map from polynomial labels to lattice observables ("its section is a fixed polynomial in compact group variables", 13ba:223). The "microscopic sections … fixed before `N,p`" of 19:28 are the sections `𝒱_d` of 11E:4–7 ("neither is chosen again when the cutoff or period changes"); the *normalized* microscopic section `O^𝒱_{N,p}(v) = a_N^{−d}𝒱_d[S_{1/t_N}v](0)` (11E:36–39) does depend on `N,p`.
  *Basis:* D (2:138–146). *Where:* 2:133–146; 2e:253; 11E:4–7, 36–39; 13:234; 13sb:15, 60; 13ba:67, 75, 217, 223; 19:28. *Proposed:* keep (a section as a right inverse is standard); recall the definition once in chapters 13 and 19. Gloss: *lattice representative of the label*.
*Across chapters:* one sense throughout. For "microscopic sections" the basis is R via 2:138–146 and 11E:4–7 (text read); 11E:31–38 does not carry it.

#### sector
*Variants:* allocation sector; actual sector; one-sector law; positive sector.
1. **Term with fixed discrete data.** One term of the decomposition of chapter 6, with the large-field set, component assignment, block trees and index `α` fixed.
   *Basis:* D (6:85–87). *Where:* 6:85–87; 8:28, 359; 9:50, 75, 81, 105, 305, 436; 9s:16, 170, 299; 10:676; 11:244, 293. *Proposed:* *term with fixed discrete data*.
2. **Reflection half.** "Positive sector": the half `1 ≤ t < h` or `0 ≤ t < h` of the torus (the positive algebra consists of the observables depending only on links with both endpoints there).
   *Basis:* D (1:244–247). *Where:* 1:244, 247, 265. *Proposed:* *positive half* ("positive algebra" is close to standard).
*Literature:* no word; "a term in the sum" over "admissible `Ω_1`" (B85e p. 258, (8): "Let us consider a term in the sum on the right-hand side"); one term of the expansion B88b (2.18), labelled by the sequences `{Ω_j}`, `{Λ_j}`, `{S_j}` and the sets `P`, `Q`, `R` (B88b p. 257: "Summation over the sequences `{S_j}` is included in the operation `T_k`, and the effective action `A_k` depends on the sequences"). An analogue of sense 1: Bałaban first resums over all `P` giving the same small-field region, and his label has no trees and no random index; v3 fixes more data. Suggested: *term of the decomposition (with fixed discrete data)*, as already proposed.
*Across chapters:* sense 2 only in chapter 1; sense 1 unchanged from chapter 6 to chapter 11 (13 lines in chapters 1, 8, 9).
*See also:* sector allocation indicators; seeded sector.

#### sector allocation indicators
*Variants:* allocation indicators.
- **Meaning.** The factors by which the integrand is decomposed into allocation sectors (6:67–89), kept as factors of the expanded integrand when the exponentials are expanded: for the selection, the weight `∏_{p∈A_f} ϑ_f(r_p^f) ∏_{p∉A_f} (1 − ϑ_f(r_p^f))` and its analogue for the block-average discrepancies, which sum to one over all selections (6:71–78), together with the condition that `A_c` is the actual coarse large-field set (6:78–79) and the tag weights of the sector. "Expand exponentials as `e^V = 1 + (e^V − 1)` and retain all sector allocation indicators" (9:81–82) says that these factors are not expanded or bounded away, so that the sum over sectors still reproduces the original integral. In v3 the weights for `A_f`, `A_n` are smooth functions, so "indicators" is exact only for `A_c`.
  *Basis:* R (9:81–82 with 6:67–89); S for the wording. *Where:* 9:81–82. *Proposed:* *the allocation weights of the sector (6:71–79)*.
  *Source:* Scott `part2/D-section.tex:105`: "The formula is used only on compatible sectors; their sum retains the exact allocation indicators"; Scott `part2/B-section.tex:908–915` (Definition "Selections and allocation sectors"): "An *allocation sector* fixes these selected tests, their assignment to connected components of their neighbourhoods, a block tree, and the frame and predictor tags."
*Literature:* see *allocation* (sense 1).
*Across chapters:* a chapter 9 name for a chapter 6 object. Not the partition-of-unity weights alone: the tags, trees and the coarse set belong to the sector as well.
*See also:* sector; allocation; allocation sector; likelihood.

#### seeded sector
*Variants:* unseeded law; seeded / unseeded.
- **Meaning.** A *seed* is a selected large-field element: a fine plaquette in `A_f`, a mismatch edge in `A_n` (with the coarse sites `A_c`, these make up the selection `A` of 6:53–64). A *seeded sector* is an allocation sector whose selection is non-empty in the region concerned; its Gaussian law has the precision, mean and set of active coordinates determined by that selection. The *unseeded law* is the Gaussian law of the sector with `A_f = A_n = ∅` and `A_c` the actual coarse large-field set, on the same forest, with all free bonds active. Both v3 sentences are negative: "It does not compare a seeded sector to an unseeded law" (6:1544); "no comparison between unrelated event indicators or a seeded and an unseeded law has been made" (9:283–284). They say that the comparison of the nonlinear and linear local laws is made only where the windows are clean, a window meeting a selected component being assigned to that component (9:278–280).
  *Basis:* S for "seed"; I for the two v3 sentences, which have no single source sentence. *Where:* 6:1544; 9:283–284. No occurrence in chapters 10–19. *Proposed:* *a sector with selected large-field elements* / *the law of the sector with empty selection*.
  *Source:* Lean `YM.Pressure.Stores`, `YM/Pressure/Seeds.lean` (definition read): three finite sets `costs` (fine plaquettes), `aisles` (coarse bonds), `flags` (coarse sites); `YM.Push.SectorMeasure.Seeded`, `YM/Push/SECTOR_MEASURE/Cells.lean` (definition read): the two-sided threshold implications with `t_f/4`, `t_f/2`, `W t_f`, `2W t_f` at every fine plaquette and coarse bond, and `flags` equal to the actual coarse large-field set; the empty selection `YM.AnalyticBridge.LocalGaussianLaws.bareStores = ⟨∅,∅,∅⟩`, `YM/AnalyticBridge/LOCAL_GAUSSIAN_LAWS/Distinct.lean` (definition read). Martin `existence/gaussian-reassembly.tex:14–17`: "The reference `A_0` is formed at the identity coarse field with no seeds and the same forest: all free bonds are active"; Martin `existence/actual-reader-dawn-selection.tex:175–177`: "fix the seed-free store: both its seed sets are empty, and its flag set is exactly the set of flags of the actual coarse field".
*Across chapters:* undefined in v3 wherever it occurs; the reading rests on the uniform meaning of "seed" in the source manuscript and the formalisation. v3 should replace "seeded"/"unseeded" by the selection `A` of 6:53–64. The "shared frame seed" of 13ba:247, 270 (auxiliary random variables) is a different use of "seed".
*See also:* shared frame seed; selected.

#### selected
*Variants:* selection; select; selects; unselected; selector.
1. **Belonging to the large-field selection.** A large-field selection is a triple `A = (A_f, A_n, A_c)` of fine plaquettes, coarse mismatch edges and coarse sites (6:49–51); as such it satisfies no condition. `A_f`, `A_n` are chosen indices; a *consistent* selection requires `r_p ≥ t_f/4`, `n_e ≥ W t_f` on them and at most `t_f/2`, `2W t_f` off them (6:54–59); `A_c` is determined by the configuration (6:62–63, 77–78). Later a "selected" large-field support, activity, component, site factor or cutoff condition is one belonging to the large-field index set of the term; "unselected" is its complement. "Selected large-field condition set `A_M`" (9:108, 440) is the selection `A = (A_f, A_n, A_c)` of the large-field component contained in the connected product `M`, and `|A_M|` in (ch09:joint-input) is its number of elements (S). The "selected site factor `X_z`" of 11R has its own entry.
   *Basis:* D (6:49–51). *Where:* ch. 6 (about 28; "unselected" 6:336, 1341, 1342, 1437); 9:108, 153, 279, 440; 11:139, 149, 151, 154, 248, 339, 425, 434, 520, 761, 923, 1933; 11R:63, 159, 170, 182, 286, 288, 301, 305, 312, 316 ("unselected" 11R:264, 313); 11E:82 (ch. 11 files about 25). *Proposed:* *large-field index triple `A`*; *belonging to `A`*. Keep it distinct from `Bad_m(U)`.
   *Source:* for `A_M`: Scott part2/D-section.tex:170 ("Large-field components are the connected components of the neighbourhoods of the selected large-field tests … Their selections `A = (A_f, A_n, A_c)` consist of the selected fine plaquettes, mismatch edges and coarse flags; each retains `exp(−κ_B β'_u t_{m+1}² |A|)` before integration"; the bound displayed there, `∫ g_A dν ≤ P_j(𝔟)(1+s_A)^{d_j} e^{−κ'_B β'_u t_{m+1}² |A|} ∏ f_a`, is (ch09:joint-input) of 9:97–104).
2. **Belonging to the one history fixed by the construction.** "Selected trajectory / schedule / history / stage requirements / block kernels / plateau": the object fixed once in chapter 10 (and, in chapters 5–7, by the construction in hand); also the graph produced by the trajectory (12:134, 139). The selected history is, for every cutoff `N` and period `p`, the sequence of densities at the levels `m ≤ N` obtained from the Wilson density at level `N` by the block steps, with the bare coupling chosen so that the level-0 coupling is the prescribed `β̄`, and satisfying at each level the bounds of the schedule (coupling in `[β̂_m/2, 2β̂_m]`, increments `β_{m+1} − β_m − κ_G log L_m` within the stage tolerance). The "selected family" (13:395) is the family of Wilson measures on that history with its insertions; the "selected level-`h` polynomial coordinates" (13ba:30) are the level-`h` coefficients of a trial in the same history, `J_h` being its coefficient map to level `h`.
   *Basis:* I from the v3 text; S for the conditions and for the assignment of 13:395 and 13ba:30. *Where:* 5:738, 858, 1378; 6:134, 165, 177, 362, 1557; 7:286, 553, 576, 667, 1202; 9:567; 10:883, 923; 11:111, 617, 1045, 1059, 1200, 1401, 1965, 2056, 2176, 2182, 2294; 11R:89; 11E:34; 12:123, 133, 134, 139, 298, 370; 13:307, 395; 13sb:50; 13ba:17, 30, 50, 195, 200, 304; 17:11; 17w:21; 17c:135; 18:172; 19:19, 31. *Proposed:* delete, or *fixed*; where the object must be named, *the history fixed in Chapter 10* and *the same family of measures*; at 13ba:30 *their scale-`h` polynomial coordinates in the same history*.
   *Source:* Lean `YM.RG.History.Selected`, YM/RG/History.lean (definition read; fields `path_shared`: path data at level `m ≤ N` independent of the period; `represents`: `Conv N p m` for `m ≤ N`, i.e. the level-`m` bounds and `β_{N,p,m} ∈ [β̂_m/2, 2β̂_m]`, definition of `Conv` read; `starts`: at level `N` zero scalar and the bare Wilson density at `β_{N,p,N}`; `steps`: for `m < N` the level-`m` density is the block transform of the level-`(m+1)` density and `|β_{m+1} − β_m − κ_G log L_m| ≤ drift`; `reaches`: `β_{N,p,0} = β̄`; `running`: for every `ε > 0`, eventually in `m`, `|β_{N,p,m} − β̂_m| ≤ ε · S.scale m`); `YM.Family` and `YM.Family.Makes`, YM/Source/Construction.lean (definitions read in part; file title "Single Wilson family"; `Makes` has the field `wilson : C.path.Selected` and further fields on the local sections, reference levels and stencils). Martin existence/actual-phase-grid-approximants.tex:11–46: "Fix the selected family `C` … We use the paid selected-history data … the coefficient transport on this history"; :136–146: "a coefficient `b_s` in the same history's coefficient transport such that `‖e_s − I_k b_s‖_1 ≤ 1/4` … `I_k` is the coefficient identification at `k`". The identification of `J_h` (13ba:30) with Martin's `I_k` is by the matching bound and is inferred.
3. **Retained component.** A component of an affine map, or of a stencil, that is kept ("selected row").
   *Basis:* R. *Where:* ch. 6 (about 11), e.g. 6:491–505, 1405, 1435. *Proposed:* *retained*.
4. **Member of a finite subfamily.** "Finite selections": finite subfamilies of activities, terms or labels ("selected `Y_i` will be disjoint", 4:456; "the absolute sum over all finite selections", 4:616); at 9:215 a choice of one term per factor.
   *Basis:* R (4:456, 616). *Where:* 4:456, 616; 9:157, 215, 637, 671, 677, 687, 890; 17m:92. *Proposed:* *subfamily*; *family*.
5. **Low-order terms kept for joint treatment.** "Selected low-order terms".
   *Basis:* R. *Where:* 9:312, 314, 319, 320, 383. *Proposed:* *the low-order terms retained*.
6. **Along a subsequence.** The choice of a subsequence, and the continuum family obtained along it.
   *Basis:* R. *Where:* 13:6, 7, 143, 172; 15:257; 17m:446; 19:38, 112. *Proposed:* *subsequence*; *the limit along the chosen subsequence*.
7. **The phase `ξ_*`.** "Selected phase" (also "chosen", 17:15; "retained", 19:117).
   *Basis:* R. *Where:* 15:301; 17:31, 351; MT:91, 93. *Proposed:* *the fixed phase `ξ_*`*.
8. **Picked out by a formula.** In particular the pairs with nonzero weight `a_h` ("Only pairs whose separation is at most `4√m ρ` are selected", 18:297).
   *Basis:* R. *Where:* 17t:419, 454; 18:297, 352, 358. *Proposed:* *pair with `a_h ≠ 0`*; *given by*.
9. **Ordinary "chosen".** A choice made inside a proof, or made by the random index `α` ("let label `z` select `Q_e^pred = Y_{e,z}`", 4:210).
   *Basis:* R. *Where:* 2:292; 2e:103; 4:160, 210, 383, 393; 8:193; 10:273, 746, 892; 11:219, 1766, 1857, 1885, 2000, 2084; 11E:30; 13sb:136; 18lp:328. *Proposed:* *chosen*; *for every value of `α`*.
*Literature:* see *large-field selection* (sense 1).
*Across chapters:* the senses change with the chapter and meet inside chapters 6, 9 and 11 (11:1933 against 11:1965; 11R:89 against 11R:159). At 4:456 and 4:616 the text (read) has finite subfamilies (sense 4), not "chosen"; 4:160 is a choice made in a proof (sense 9). Two assignments are not decided by the v3 text and are settled by the sources: 13:395 "the same selected family" is sense 2 (the one family of Wilson measures on the fixed history; no subsequence is involved), and 13ba:30 "selected level-`h` polynomial coordinates" is sense 2 (the level-`h` coefficients in that history). Sense 2 has a precise content in the sources and in the formalisation (Lean `YM.RG.History.Selected`), which v3 states in chapter 10 without attaching it to the word. Counts: 48 occurrences of `select*` in chapter 6 with "unselected" (44 without; split 28 / 11 / 5 not recounted); 26 lines in chapters 1, 2, 7–9; 5 / 30 / 12 / 3 in files 10 / 11 / 11R / 11E; 23 in chapters 12–16; 19 in chapters 17–19.
*See also:* selected site factor `X_z`; selected slot; stationary graph; subtraction convention.

#### selected site factor `X_z`
- **Meaning.** `X_z = exp[−β(d_z + b'_z)]`, the factor attached to a site `z` of the selected large-field set, built from the local energy contributions `d_z`, `b'_z`.
  *Basis:* D (11R:96–116). *Where:* 11R:96–116, 159–162, 170. *Proposed:* keep (it is defined).
*Across chapters:* 11R only; "selected" in sense 1 of *selected*.
*See also:* selected.

#### selected slot
*Variants:* forced slot, marked slot (source).
- **Meaning.** The place of one large-field activity in the polymer representation of the step, identified by its index: the support of the activity together with its prescribed set of large-field sites and its conditions. A large-field remainder of an insertion sits in one such place, where the activity is replaced by the factor carrying the insertion. "Its selected slot has no purely principal component" (11:424) says that in the expansion around that factor there is no term consisting of small-field (principal) factors only, because the factor carrying the insertion is itself a large-field factor; hence no principal bound is needed and only the nonprincipal and large-field estimates apply.
  *Basis:* S (11:424 gives no gloss). *Where:* 11:424. *Proposed:* *The large-field factor carrying the insertion gives no purely principal term*; for the noun, *the index (support and prescribed set of large-field sites) of the large-field activity carrying the insertion*.
  *Source:* Martin existence/heading-history-handoff.tex:313–321 ("For an allowed forced slot `s`, let `f ≠ 0` be its local, gauge-invariant measurable insertion, with the slot's support and eligibility conditions … Its input profile equals `f` at the original support–inventory address and zero at every other address. It has no ordinary principal cluster: the marked slot is flagged, whereas that cluster requires an ordinary insertion. The nonprincipal and forced bounds thus give the zero-leading-coefficient bound without a principal bound"). Lean `YM.Source.Coefficient` with field `forced : ℕ → Config G n → ℂ`, `YM.Source.Coefficient.marked`, `YM.Source.Coefficient.Format` with fields `forcing`, `carried`, `supported` (YM/Source/Insertion.lean:27–61; definitions read: `marked R b U = Σ_{i∈b} forced i U · ∏_{j∈b.erase i} K_j U` on admissible `b`, and `forced i` is tied to the `i`-th large-field address of the representation). The structure `ForcedAddress` itself was not opened.
*Across chapters:* one occurrence. This is a third sense of *slot*, distinct from the strips of chapter 1 and from the argument positions of chapters 13–18. The word "selected" there is counted under sense 1 of *selected*.
*See also:* slot.

#### separate quadratic correction
- **Meaning.** The term `Σ A_i^(2)` of the path action that is not multiplied by `β` (4:517), which 4:525 calls "the separate quadratic correction"; it is the quadratic part `ℒ` of `P^path_{N,m}(β,U) = β𝒦(U) + ℒ(U)` (9:21–28). "The separate loop correction is not part of the classical metric" (6:170).
  *Basis:* R (4:517, 525; 9:21–28). *Where:* 4:517, 525; 6:170. *Proposed:* *`β`-independent quadratic term `ℒ` of the path action*.
*Across chapters:* a chapter 4 name for the object called "inherited (quadratic) loop action" and "loop correction" elsewhere.
*See also:* inherited loop action.

#### separated
*Variants:* separated test function; separated correlation, configuration, word, response, bound, smearing.
- **Meaning.** At pairwise distinct points, respectively supported away from coincident points: "A separated test function is an element of `C_c^∞(Conf_n)`, extended by zero to `(ℝ⁴)^n`" (1:359). 14:17–18 states the convention without the word ("evaluated at distinct points or against test functions supported away from collisions").
  *Basis:* D (1:359) for test functions; R otherwise. *Where:* 1:359; ch. 3, about a dozen (3:104, 144–145, 494, 802, 1015); ch. 12–16, 63; ch. 17–19, MT, RG, about 28 (e.g. 18:20). *Proposed:* keep; recall the definition once in chapter 13.
*Across chapters:* one sense throughout.
*See also:* separation.

#### separated test function
See *separated*.

#### separating family
*Variants:* finite separating family; separating families; free separating family; quantitative separating families; detecting family (14:221); (labels only) detector.
- **Meaning.** A finite family of correlation functionals, each the correlation with fixed insertions at fixed points, that is injective on a space of fields. Chapter 3 gives two: for a basis `(P_1, …, P_s)` of `M_d^Max` and fixed distinct points `x, y`, the map `P ↦ (S_2^Max(P, P_j; x, y))_{j=1}^s` is injective (Corollary "Polynomial positivity and finite separating families", 3:484–495); and there is a finite `D_*` with `𝒩_{D_*} ∩ 𝔓^G = {0}`, where `𝒩_D` is the set of polynomials whose correlations with every separated word of insertions `P_i ∈ M_D^Max` vanish (Proposition "A separating family of insertions of bounded scaling dimension", 3:797–809). Later chapters estimate the interacting correlations along such a family and call the result "the bound from a finite separating family" (11:29; 11E:183); "A common localization map for the separating family" (11:1141) is the map `T`; "bounded lifts of the separating family" (15:256) are polynomial preimages of its free fields.
  *Basis:* R (3:484–495, 797–809): the term stands in the two titles and the statements give its meaning; no sentence defines it. *Where:* 3:484, 775–779, 806; 11:29, 986, 1078, 1097, 1141, 1348, 1587; 11E:170, 183; 13:14, 395; 14:221 ("detecting families"), 832; 15:17, 250, 256; 19:27, 52, 99. *Proposed:* keep *separating family*, defined once in chapter 3; use it also for "detecting families" (14:221), "detection" (3:830; 11:960, 976; 11E:171) and "rank detection" (13sb:9).
  *Source:* Scott `part2/E-section.tex:493–499`: "Choose finitely many one- or two-point tests. In test `i`, the first label is the variable `𝔪_j`; the optional second label is a fixed basis element. … The free test matrix is `𝒢_{ij} = S^Max_{n_i}(𝔪_j, test i spectator; y^i)`. The next lemma supplies a finite family that distinguishes every free field of degree at most `d`. Lemma (Free tests). … there are finitely many one- or two-point tests at generic configurations, with every second label a basis element, for which the matrix has rank `dim_ℂ 𝓜_d`"; Scott `part2/H-section.tex:160`: "Each row of trial `ℓ` consists of a singleton `u` and optional spectator `v`, placed at the comparison points `r_ℓ y^{ℓ,i}`."
*Across chapters:* one sense from chapter 3 to chapter 19. Not *nondegeneracy*: the text's own word is "separating family" (3:484, 806), which is kept. "Separated" (at pairwise distinct points, 1:359; 3:104, 144–145) is a different word and stays. The members of the family are functionals; the probes of chapter 18 are the words that define such functionals, and the "reference rows" of 15:278 are the tests of the finite free family, which index the rows of the matrix of these pairings (see *row*, sense 8). The source states the family in this matrix form: for a real basis `𝔪_1 = 1, 𝔪_2, …` of the free field space, finitely many one- or two-point tests at generic configurations, each with a variable first label and an optional fixed second label, such that the matrix `𝒢_{ij}` of free correlations of `𝔪_j` in test `i` has rank equal to the dimension of the space.
*See also:* detection; detector; detecting family; probe; reference rows; separation; separated; spectator; lift; top polynomial extraction.

#### separation
1. **Displacement `x − y`.**
   *Basis:* I. *Where:* 3:61, 431. *Proposed:* *displacement*.
2. **The separating property of a family of functionals.** "Separates", "separating family" (3:484, 775, 779, 806); the property is used at 3:973, 981.

3. **Of singularities.**

4. **Mutual distance of points.** The distance between insertion points or between a cluster and the exterior word ("with pairwise separation and slab margins at least `r`", 14:99; "pairs whose separation is at most `4√m ρ`", 18:297; "exterior separation", 18r).
   *Basis:* R (14:99; 18:297). *Where:* 11:868, 1130, 1895, 2080, 2189; 14:99; 18:297; "exterior separation" in 18r:9–12, 33, 36. *Proposed:* *distance*.

#### shared frame seed
*Variants:* frame seed; frame seeds; shared seeds.
- **Meaning.** The auxiliary random variable by which the gauge frame at a coarse site is chosen in one block step. The block kernel is a mixture over a finite label `α` of "all frame and block average choices", with joint probability `λ(U,α)`; "Frame choices are made first, followed by conditionally independent block average choices" (4:217–219). 13ba realises these choices by "independent primitive random variables … for each coarse-link sample" (13ba:230–232); the variable for a frame is its *seed*. It is *shared* because the frame at a site enters every coarse link issuing from that site, so that coarse links are not conditionally independent given the fine field: "This does not assert that coarse links remain conditionally independent after a shared frame choice has been averaged out. The full cones, including that choice, must be disjoint" (13ba:240–242). Hence the ancestor cone of a stencil must contain "every input link and every shared frame seed for an output link" (13ba:247), which lie within distance `(j_i+7)a_i` of its initial endpoint (13ba:248).
  *Basis:* R (13ba:229–242, 247; 4:217–219). *Where:* 13ba:231, 247, 270. *Proposed:* *the random variable choosing the frame at a coarse site* (*auxiliary random variables of the block step* for the collection).
*Across chapters:* 13ba only. It is unrelated to "seeded / unseeded" (6:1544; 9:283): there a seed is a selected large-field element (see *seeded sector*); here it is a source of randomness. The term and the requirement come from the review of the v3 draft, not from a source manuscript: `audit/bounded-coarse-approximation-review.md` item 1 ("Conditional factorization requires full random-seed cones. The actual block kernel is a mixture over shared frame choices, not a product in coarse links conditional only on the fine field. Include the independent frame seeds, predictor seeds, and link-noise seeds … in each ancestor cone"), recorded there as a correction to Scott part2/E-bounded-real.tex:23, which has only "the block kernels are products in the coarse-link variables given the preceding field". No Lean declaration was matched.
*See also:* seeded sector.

#### shares
*Variants:* shares `p_{xa}`; share.
- **Meaning.** The weights `p_{xa} = 1_{X_a}(x)/|X_a|`, summing to one over `x`, by which a term `f_a^0` is distributed over the sites of its support ("Give an ordinary selected term `f_a^0` the shares …, and a path term the share …", 9:314).
  *Basis:* D (9:314–316). *Where:* 9:314–316, 323. *Proposed:* *weights*.
*Across chapters:* chapter 9 only (4 occurrences of `share` in chapters 1, 2, 7–9).

#### shell
1. **On shell.** Restricted to jets of solutions ("on-shell polynomial space").
   *Basis:* R (3:166). *Where:* 3:149, 166, 213, 216, 341, 552, 588. *Proposed:* keep (standard).
2. **Support of the gradient of a cutoff.** The annular region `supp ∇χ` through which a flux is taken: "shell flux", "shell integrals", "shell identity", "stress shell", "total shell response" (14:796), said of `−∫∂_μV_c S(J_{μc}, A)` (14:776–777), which the text calls a response, not a flux.
   *Basis:* R (3:666–672; 14:776–777). *Where:* 3:546; 14:312 (title "Shrinking shells and local charge fields"), 384, 395, 404, 776, 796, 825, 1014; 15:245; 16:538, 558; 17:99; 17w:122. The flux itself is defined at 3:666–672 and 14:318–322, where the word is not used; at 14:328–330 it is only in the name of the figure `ward-shell`. *Proposed:* *flux of the current through the shell `supp ∇χ`*; *the flux integral*.
3. **Shell factor.** The power `ρ^{3+ϰ}` by which the cancelling coefficients are multiplied (formula at 14:340; the phrase at 14:358).
   *Basis:* R (14:358). *Where:* 14:358. *Proposed:* *the factor `ρ^{3+ϰ}`*.
4. **Region of comparable size.** The region where `ρ` is comparable to one value ("A single shell", "one-shell estimate"), in the tree vocabulary for nested collision subsets; similarly the dyadic energy range "On the shell `u/2 < E ≤ u`" (16:415).
   *Basis:* I (18:406–418); R at 16:415. *Where:* 18:406, 413, 418; 16:415. *Proposed:* *the region `ρ ≤ |…| ≤ 2ρ`*; at 16:415 *the range `u/2 < E ≤ u`*.
5. **Lattice shell sum.** `sup_v Σ_i e^{−η d(v,a_i)}`; similarly "roots in shell `j`" (11:269), sites at distance of order `j`.
   *Basis:* R. *Where:* 5:1212; 11:269. *Proposed:* print the sum.
6. **Mass shell** (standard physics term). "Mass-shell Laplace kernels" `K_{m,k,h}` (17:424–426), "mass-shell polynomial comparison" (17:455), "mass-shell correlation functions" (MT:102).
   *Basis:* R (17:424–426). *Where:* 17:424, 455; 19:123; MT:102. *Proposed:* keep (standard).
*Across chapters:* six unrelated uses: sense 1 in chapter 3; sense 2 in chapters 3, 14, 15, 16, 17 (one sense, the shell `supp ∇χ`); sense 3 in chapter 14; sense 4 in chapters 16 and 18; sense 5 in chapters 5 and 11; sense 6 in chapters 17, 19 and the main theorem. For sense 2, not *smeared charge of the current*: it contradicts `blueprint/notation.md` ("integral of a conserved-current correlation against an annular cutoff derivative") and names a different object.

#### shell factor
See *shell* (sense 3).

#### shooting
*Variants:* shooting parameter.
- **Meaning.** The choice of the bare coupling at cutoff level `N` so that the finite trajectory ends at the prescribed coarse value: `β_{N,p,0} = β̄` (10:243–251); "shooting from the Wilson measure gives its bare coupling `β_{N,p,N}` with prescribed coarse endpoint `β̄`" (19:21–23). The section 10:209 ff. is titled "Tuning a finite history to the coarse endpoint".
  *Basis:* R (19:21–23). *Where:* 10:273, 818; 19:21–23. *Proposed:* *tuning of the bare coupling* (MT:62 already says "tune"); "shooting" is acceptable with one sentence, as in the shooting method for boundary-value problems.
*Literature:* unnamed in Bałaban: the existence of a bare coupling with prescribed coupling at the unit scale, part of the "coupling constant renormalization" (B87 p. 259, Theorem 2: "there exists a bare coupling constant g_0 = g_0(ε,g) such that the sequence of the effective coupling constants g_k is contained in the interval ]0,γ], and g_K = g"; its proof is deferred, "will be given in a separate paper"); **tuning**, "non-perturbative renormalization" (D1 p. 1330010-42: "To accomplish this tuning we do not at first specify the initial values for ε_k, μ_k but instead specify final values … This is non-perturbative renormalization"; p. 1330010-41, footnote: "This section is not particularly due to Balaban"). The same object (the same statement). v3 proves it by an intermediate-value argument (10:232–251), D1 by a contraction on sequences with prescribed final values. "Shooting" is not used in any paper read. Suggested: *tuning of the bare coupling by prescribing the coupling at the unit scale (B87 Theorem 2)*.
*Across chapters:* one sense; 19:21–23 is an explicit sentence (text read), hence basis R.

#### signed
1. **Signed coordinate permutations.** Coordinate permutations combined with reflections (the lattice symmetry group): "signed symmetry orbit", "signed-coordinate symmetry", "signed orientation".
   *Basis:* R. *Where:* 1:218–220; 6:966; 7:195; 13ba:60; 14:26; 14lc:8. *Proposed:* keep (standard).
2. **With its sign kept.** The difference itself, before absolute values are taken, so that cancellations survive: "the signed residual must be transported on the same history … Taking absolute values before that subtraction loses the cancellation" (18:129–131); "The sign of the local difference has been retained throughout" (18lp:65); "Signed regular costs" against "the absolute activity site sum" (13sb:35–36).
   *Basis:* R (18:129–131); I for 13sb:35. *Where:* 13sb:35; 18lp:24, 65, 197; 18:129, 158, 174, 248, 255, 413; 18r:21, 26; RG:73. *Proposed:* *the difference itself (not its absolute value)*.
3. **Of either sign.** "The corrected dyadic profile is signed" (14:681); "the signed equality" `Resp_i = −Resp_j` (14:520); "the two signed defects" (6:213), "the two signed mismatch terms" (6:1410).
   *Basis:* R (14:681). *Where:* 6:213, 1410; 14:520, 681. *Proposed:* *not of definite sign*.
*Across chapters:* sense 1 in chapters 1, 6, 7, 13, 14; sense 2 in chapters 13 and 18; sense 3 in chapters 6 and 14. 13sb:35, read with its neighbouring "absolute", is sense 2 (text read).
*See also:* signed local transport.

#### signed local transport
- **Meaning.** A nickname, cited once ("Its construction requires the signed local transport, the stronger anchored marked support bound, and the graded quotient comparison", 18:172–175), for the estimate (18.signed-transport) of the subsection of the same title (18lp:24–65). A local degree-`t` marked density at level `l` is a column with coefficient `x_l` plus a remainder whose extracted coefficient is zero and whose remainder norm is at most `r_l`; the densities at successive levels of a sufficiently late interval `[k_*, m]` are related by one marked step, `H_l = L_l^t 𝓑_l H_{l+1}`. If a free column parameter at the fine end `m` is chosen so that `x_{k_*} = 0`, then `r_l + |x_l|_1 ≤ 4(1+C_m) q_fin (a_m/a_l)^{1/8}` for `k_* ≤ l ≤ m` and `r_m ≤ 2(1+C_m) q_fin`, where `q_fin` is the combined coefficient and remainder bound of the original density at level `m`, before the column is subtracted. "Signed" is sense 2 of *signed*: the column is subtracted from the density as an equality of densities, before norms are taken ("The sign of the local difference has been retained throughout", 18lp:65; cf. 18:129–131).
  *Basis:* R (18lp:24, the subsection title; 18lp:48–55, the estimate). *Where:* 18:174; 18lp:24 (title). *Proposed:* *the estimate (18.signed-transport)*, cited by number. If a noun is wanted, moving a quantity through the block steps is *transfer* in this book, not *transport*.
  *Source:* Scott `part2/J-section.tex:45–56`: "The next estimate retains the signed difference produced by subtracting a column. A transported family on `[k_*,m]` is a sequence of local marked expressions `c_l(b_l)+R_l`, `k_* ≤ l ≤ m`, in which `R_l` has coefficient zero and each term arises from the next finer one by one marked integration step … Its measured coefficient is `x_l = C_l b_l`, and `r_l` is its remainder bound"; Lemma "Signed local transport" (`lem:J-signed-local`), part (b): "If `x_{k_*} = 0`, then, for `k_* ≤ l ≤ m`, `r_l + μ(x_l) ≤ 4(1+C_m) q_fin (a_m/a_l)^{1/8}`, `r_m ≤ 2(1+C_m) q_fin`". Lean `YM.Bid.G09` (`YM/Bid/Loan.lean:133–136`; statement read), proved as `YM.Work.G09.answer` (`YM/Work/G09.lean:224`): for a `YM.Bid.Duet` on the levels `[k,o]` satisfying `YM.Bid.Duet.Woke` with parameter `w ≥ 0` (`Loan.lean:105–126`; definitions read: exact density relation between consecutive levels, zero coefficient at level `k`, `cost o ≤ w + C_o(w + |x_o|)`), and under the stage inequalities `roomCost`, `Bank` (`Loan.lean:36–46`; definitions read), `gainChart H o i · (cost i + |x_i|) ≤ 4(1+C_o) w` for `k ≤ i ≤ o`, where `gainChart H o i = exp((1/8)(scale o − scale i)) = (a_i/a_o)^{1/8}`; `YM.Work.G09.cost_finest` (`G09.lean:210–213`; statement read): `cost o ≤ 2(1+C_o) w`; `YM.Work.G09.cone_cost` (`G09.lean:183–188`; statement read): `32(1+C_i)² |x_i| ≤ cost i`, the cone of 18lp:61. The hypotheses `direction`, `Format`, `remBound` of `Woke` were not opened.
*Across chapters:* one occurrence of the nickname; the constants `4(1+C_m)`, `2(1+C_m)`, the exponent `1/8` and the cone constant `32(1+C)²` agree in v3, Scott and Lean.
*See also:* signed; transfer; anchored marked support bound; graded quotient comparison.

#### site bound
See *site conversion*.

#### site conversion
*Variants:* root-to-site conversion; support conversion, support conversions; support conversion cost `T_l`; support conversion constants.
1. **Site conversion (root-to-site conversion).** The passage from a bound for supports anchored (rooted) at a point to a bound for supports containing a given site, at the cost of one unit of the support exponent and a factor `𝒲(B)`: "The conversion of anchored bounds to containing-site bounds is explicit … An additional exponent in the support weight absorbs this polynomial" (9:513–517); "The site bound is `Σ` at exponent `v+1`. To see the latter conversion, root a support at one of its actual fine sites or marks …" (11:266–272); "Root-to-site conversion costs only `𝒲(B)`" (11:1918).
   *Basis:* R (9:513–517; 11:266–272, 1918). *Where:* 9:513; 11:267, 502, 1918; 13ba:145. *Proposed:* *passage from anchored to containing-site bounds*.
2. **Support conversion.** The change of the exponential support weight from one cover radius or level to another: `e^{(v+2)c_{B_c}(X^↑)} ≤ T_e e^{σ_f c_{B_f}(X)}` with `T_e = exp(15⁴(e+7))` ((ch11:cover-transfer), 11:228–238), from the fine cover number at radius `B_f` to the coarse cover number of the enlarged support. "Its full support conversion cost is `T_l ≤ L_l`, as in (ch11:cover-transfer)" (18lp:112–113). `T_e` is the constant of this step, not the cost of sense 1. In 11R the plural covers this and sense 1 together: "Eventually its old exponent absorbs this new exponent and the extra unit used to turn an anchored bound into a site bound. These are the support conversions" (11R:140–143).
   *Basis:* R (11:228–238; 18lp:112–113; 11R:140–143). *Where:* 11:515, 527–528; 11R:142, 281, 320–321; 18lp:112–113. *Proposed:* *change of cover radius, (ch11:cover-transfer)*.
*Across chapters:* two operations: sense 1 in chapters 9, 11 and 13ba, sense 2 in chapter 11, 11R and 18lp; 13ba and 18lp use them without explanation and are settled by chapters 9 and 11 (11:226–238, 264–272 read). "Site bound" and "site sum" are the sums over the terms containing a site and belong under *containing-site bound*. The "incidence" bounds of chapter 11 (sum over terms containing a given insertion) are contrasted with the site bound.
*See also:* incidence; containing-site bound; connected covering number.

- **Meaning.** The six local terms `E_f, E_n, E_c, E_N, E_L, E_D` (6:190–200), each evaluated at a plaquette, edge or complement-component anchor, whose sum over the torus is `ΣK_f + (b/2)Σ n_e² − ΣK_c` (6:205–208). The local energy `𝓔_A` is their sum over the anchors in `A^{[2B]}` (6:210–212).

#### slab
*Variants:* slab word; slab insertion; slab operator `B_h(w)`; reflected slab word `w^♯`; slab bounds; slab width; slab margins; slab kernel.
- **Meaning.** "A word `w` lies in a slab of width `h` if `0 < x_i^μ < h` for each of its points. Its reflected slab word is `w^♯ = τ_hθ_μ w`" (14:86–88). Slab operators are the operators `B_h(w)` built from such words (14:97–104). The "slab margins" of 14:99 ("with pairwise separation and slab margins at least `r`") are the distances of the times `x_i^μ` from the two faces of the slab; they are one component of the *buffer* of 13:335, not the whole of it (text read). In chapter 11 a "slab kernel" is one of the factors `B_i` of a transfer word `tr ∏ B_i T^{H_i}/Z`, the slab having width `w` (11:842–845).
  *Basis:* D (14:86–88, 97–104); R for the slab kernel (11:842–845). *Where:* 13:335, 391 (before the definition); 14:83–141; ch. 15; 16:35–37 (24 in chapters 12–16); 18:270; 19:92, 103; RG:44. Also 11:844–846, 876 ("`B_i` is a local slab kernel, the slab width is `w`"; "reflected-copy bound for a slab"). *Proposed:* keep; move the definition before 13:335 or refer forward.
*Across chapters:* one sense from chapter 13 on. That the slabs of the transfer words of 11:844–876 are the same notion is inferred.
*See also:* buffer; strip; transfer word.

*Variants:* slots; one-slot response; selected slot.

   *Basis:* R (1:314–315). *Where:* 1:314. *Proposed:* *factors of the cyclic product* (it is not certain that a standard word exists).
2. **Argument position.** An argument of a correlation or of a multilinear weight ("permuted with the slots", 18:299; "one-slot response" `L_{v,f}(c)`, 13:119–122).
   *Basis:* R. *Where:* 13:120, 132; 14:172, 220; 14lc:46; 15:115; 16:239; 18:299. *Proposed:* *argument*.
3. **Index of a large-field activity.** The place (support with prescribed set of large-field sites) of one large-field activity of the polymer representation, at which a large-field remainder of an insertion is put; see *selected slot*.
   *Basis:* S. *Where:* 11:424. *Proposed:* *index of the large-field activity*.

#### small-coordinate event
- **Meaning.** The complement of the large-coordinate event `ℰ_w = {∃i: d(i,w) ≤ 2B, |z_i| ≥ T}`, `T = ξ t_f/(2g)` (6:837–843): "On the small-coordinate event, `v = m_Y + gz` has size `O(t_f)`" (6:897). The large-coordinate event is the event outside which a cutoff remainder vanishes ("Its smallness comes from a large-coordinate event", 6:834–835).
  *Basis:* R (6:837–843, 897). *Where:* 6:897. *Proposed:* *the complement of the large fluctuation-field event `{|z_i| ≥ T for some i near w}`*; `ℰ_w` is not called "large-field event" without "fluctuation".
*Literature:* see *cutoff failure* (sense 1); the complement is the small fluctuation field condition, `χ_k`, `χ^w_k`.
*Across chapters:* chapter 6 only. These Gaussian-tail events are distinct from the large-field selection `A` and from `Bad_m(U)`.
*See also:* cutoff remainder; large-coordinate event; selected.

#### smooth representative `W_a`
See *stationary tangent*. `W_a = W_s − d_{0,f}ERW_s` (5:1108) is a representative of the stationary tangent chosen for its fine-difference bounds; it is not the derivative of the stationary map, which is the forest representative `W_F` (5:1147–1150).
*Literature:* see *stationary tangent*.

#### smoothing order
*Variants:* smoothing order `j`, `j_i`; averaging order.
- **Meaning.** The number of box convolutions in the averaging weight of the block average: "fix a positive integer smoothing order `j`" (4:16). The endpoint frames then read a box of fine-lattice radius `(j_i+3)L_i` (13ba:244–245).
  *Basis:* D (4:16). *Where:* 4:16, 186; 5:196–202, 303–305 ("averaging orders"); 7:600, 664 (`C_j`, inferred); 10:124 (`ȷ_j`); 13ba:229–248; 17m:230, 239, 251. *Proposed:* keep *smoothing order `j`*, defined once (4:16).
*Literature:* name clash; the object itself has no counterpart, since in all papers read the averaging weight is uniform over one block, `L^{-d}`. In Bałaban the **order** of a block, of an averaging operator or of a renormalization transformation is the number of composed steps: "block of an order j" (B85a p. 17), "k-th order averaging" (B85a p. 24: "if k-th order averaging `Ū^k` is defined at bonds of Ω^(k), then `Ū^{k+1} = \overline{(Ū^k)}`"), "averaging operators of different orders", "renormalization transformations of different orders" (B84b p. 223), "block of k-th order `B^k(y)`" (B87 p. 267). "Order of the averaging kernel" for `j` would therefore be misread. Adopted (23 November 2026): keep *smoothing order `j`*, defined at 4:16 as the number of box convolutions in the averaging weight; the earlier proposal "order of the averaging kernel" is withdrawn, for the reason just given. The letter `j` clashes with the stage index.
*Across chapters:* one sense. The letter `j` is also the stage index (chapter 9; defined 10:25); chapter 10 writes `ȷ_j` for "the largest smoothing order used in stage `j`" (10:124). That the `j` of chapter 7 is the smoothing order at every occurrence is inferred.
*See also:* stage.

#### source
1. **Source variable.** The nilpotent variables `z_i` (`z_i² = 0`) of the source algebra, generating variables for the insertions; "linear in the sources", "source monomial `z_S`", "source degree".
   *Basis:* D (11:33–40). *Where:* 11:49, 133–134, 507, 509, 1324, 1384, 1458, 1477, 1487, 1493, 1577, 1584, 1881, 1891, 2129 (about 16); 11E:144; ch. 12 (14); 13sb:11, 66, 67; 13ba (9); 14lc:53, 57; 18lp:9, 69, 210; 17m:440; 18:125. *Proposed:* *source variable `z_i`* (keep).
2. **Source weight.** See *source weight*.
3. **Source algebra.** See *squarefree source algebra*.
4. **The inserted factor itself.** The source polynomial, the inserted observable or its density ("complete source", "terminal source", "corrected source", "source density `q_k`", "physical source"); an insertion ("local sources", "source anchors"); in `17-marked-trace-rates.tex` the inserted differentiated-kernel factor `𝒟_Y k` ("full source", "zero-moment source", "score source") and the "regular (local) sources", the local expressions (`div_Haar Y − D𝓛[Y]` etc.) whose Taylor coefficient is extracted.
   *Basis:* R. *Where:* 10:173, 178; 11:133, 769, 1632, 1671, 2097, 2140; 11E:84; 13sb:65, 72; 13ba:123, 158, 284; 18lp:29, 180; 17m:68, 155, 391, 400, 412, 443, 459; 17m:193, 265, 291, 303, 307. *Proposed:* *insertion*; in 17m *the differentiated kernel `𝒟_Y k`*.
5. **Inhomogeneous term.** `b_Y`, the inhomogeneous term of the affine map of chapter 6, with `f_Y = D*b_Y` the linear coefficient of the quadratic form; and the inhomogeneous term of a linear recursion ("No constant source term"; also "forcing").
   *Basis:* R (6:448–449, 581–612; 17c:132). *Where:* 6:448–449, 581–612; 9:924 ("clipped frozen source"); 10:900; 11R:43; 17c:132, 225, 245 ("forcing" 17c:380, 382, 385, 386). *Proposed:* *inhomogeneous term*; *linear coefficient* for `f_Y`.
6. **Generating-function source.** The parameters `t_j` of the polymer gas with sources; the linear source of a two-point function (3:409 ff.).
   *Basis:* R. *Where:* 3:409; 8:252, 266, 268, 364. *Proposed:* keep (standard).
7. **The text the book was written from.** "Source locations" (RG:82), "the source prescription" (18:411) and "the source construction" (14:186), the construction of the manuscript the chapter was written from, with the parameters `r_k = a_kM_k^{α_0}`, … of Scott part2/G-section.tex (see *source construction*).
   *Basis:* I (R via `notation.md` for 18:411; S for 14:186, under *source construction*). *Where:* 14:186; 18:411; RG:82. *Proposed:* name the underlying text once, or remove the reference.
8. **Pertaining to insertions.** "Source attachment", "source constants", "corrected-source estimate" (settled by 14lc:48–55: the estimate for the corrected coefficients `R_I`).
   *Basis:* R / I. *Where:* 13sb:15, 63, 73; 14lc:45, 69; 18lp:148. *Proposed:* *of the insertions*.
*Literature:* "density of a generating functional for the correlation functions", obtained by adding `⟨g, φ⟩` to the exponent (B95 p. 108: "we consider a density of a generating functional for the correlation functions, which means simply that we add the linear function ⟨g, φ⟩ to the exponent"; D3 p. 2171: "The analysis can be adapted to treat correlation functions as well"). A weak analogue of sense 1 and of the vocabulary of insertions and marked or unmarked terms: an ordinary source `g`, nothing nilpotent, no marked/unmarked distinction. Suggested: *generating functional with sources* for the idea; keep v3's words for the nilpotent version.
*Across chapters:* the senses change with the chapter: sense 5 in chapters 6, 9, 17c; sense 6 in chapters 3, 8; senses 1–4 and 8 from chapter 10 on; sense 7 in three places. 11:1632 ("a principal source term") is sense 4: a prescribed principal term `F_{c,I}`, for a cell `c` and a set `I` of its insertions, "the desired principal source at mode `(c,I)`" of the source (Martin existence/allarity-marked-propagation.tex:103–115, where the estimate of 11:1632–1633 reads "The incidence bound of these new regular remainders is at most `2^n ω̄_n R_e y`"; see *principal*, sense 4). 17w:12, 78 ("polynomial-source propagation constants", "regular and large-field source recurrences") are sense 8: the recurrences for the bounds of the terms carrying insertions (see *polynomial-source propagation constants*). 9:168 is ordinary. Counts: 6 in chapters 1, 2, 7–9; 3 / 36 / 1 / 2 in files 10 / 11 / 11R / 11E; 49 in chapters 12–16; 21 in chapters 17–19.
*See also:* source construction; source locations; source prescription; source weight; squarefree source algebra.

What that source is, is not said in the reading guide.

Work in this directory is an editorial and mathematical reconstruction of those sources". `blueprint/scott-trish-comparison.md:1–3`: "Scott–Trish source comparison. Byte comparison, with changed-line counts … Identical files need not be read twice" (the table lists the same file names for both, e.g. `part1/01-result.tex` "different, 16 / 10"); `blueprint/source-index.md` indexes the files as `Scott/…`, `Trish/…`; `audit/chapter-11.md:8–9` cites "Trish E-Gaussian-sources.tex, lem:E-course-mass", "Trish E-several-mark.tex, lem:E-joint-terminal". The Trish files are not in the checkout under `manuscript/` (only `existence/` and `HumanizeYM_v2/` are), so their text was not read. A word search for "Lean" in `audit/*.md` finds it only in `chapters-01-02.md` and `foundations-literature.md` (and in this dictionary).

The coefficient of `z_S` is then bounded by a quantity divided by `∏ω_i` (12:243–244; display 11:808–811). "Marker amplitude `e^{2q}`" (14lc:61) appears to be the same weight (inferred).

#### sparse stopping scale
*Variants:* sparse stopping; sparse-stopping argument.
- **Meaning.** The stopping scale is the level `k = k(m)`, "the first level `k ≥ m` with `B_k² ≤ a_m/a_k`" (13sb:104–105), for which `(a_m/a_k)⁴ q_k^site ≤ (L_{k−1}B_{k−1}²)⁴ q_k^site = o(τ_k)` (13sb:104–109); the last condition of the schedule (10:167–172) is imposed so as to "keep replication costs subpower at a nearby sparse stopping scale". "Nearby" is `τ_k/τ_m → 1` (13sb:117). "Sparse" refers to the grid of reflected insertions seen from level `k`: one insertion per cell of the reflected tiling of scale `a_m`, so that at level `k` the insertions ("reflected anchors") are `a_m/a_k ≥ B_k²` lattice units apart (13sb:85–86), far more than the support radius `B_k`. The condition `B_k² ≤ a_m/a_k` is the definition of a *stopping pair* `(m,k)` in the source.
  *Basis:* R for the level (13sb:104–109); S for "sparse", with I for the last step: the source says "sparse insertion grids" and gives the spacing, but no sentence defines "sparse stopping scale". *Where:* 10:172; 18lp:159 (which refers to 13sb:104–117). *Proposed:* *the scale `k(m)` of (13sb:104)*; drop "sparse", or say *at which the reflected insertions are at least `B_k²` lattice units apart*.
  *Source:* Scott part2/E-section.tex:111–117: "The following choice gives both the sparse insertion grids and the windows used for free comparison", followed by Lemma "Scale and period choices", whose last requirement is `(a_m/a_{k(m)})^4 q_{k(m)} = o(s_{k(m)})`; part2/E-several-mark.tex:188, 208: "A stopping pair is a pair of levels `m ≤ k` with `B_k² ≤ a_m/a_k`"; "The reflected anchors at level `k` have spacing `a_m/a_k ≥ B_k²` … Since `B_{i+1}² ≤ 2B_i²` and `ℓ_i ≥ 3`, their spacing is at least `B_i²` at every finer level"; part2/E-section.tex:362: "the stopping level `k = k(m)` of Lemma E1.1; the choice of `k(m)` makes the per-cell site cost negligible against `s_k`".
*Across chapters:* a forward reference in chapter 10 (10:169–172, with the "Haar-ball normalization argument" and the "replication costs") settled by chapters 11 and 13. Martin's text does not use "sparse" in this sense. No Lean declaration was searched for.
*See also:* Haar-ball normalization argument; replication costs; stopping.

#### spectator
*Variants:* spectator fields, list, legs; spectator word; exterior spectator; quadratic spectator.
1. **The other insertions in a correlation.** The insertions (fields, word) other than the distinguished one, against which a correlation is evaluated: in a correlation `S(A, x; B, y)` of two concatenated lists, the list `B` at the points `y`, kept at a fixed distance from the points `x`. Two labels represent the same field when their correlations with every spectator list agree. Never defined in v3. From 3:837 the "quadratic spectator" is brought close to `P`, so it is not passive there.
   *Basis:* I. *Where:* 3:705, 782, 824–873; 11:1029, 2093, 2182, 2276; 11E:74–75, 163, 169; ch. 12–16, 33 (13: 10; 18gq: 2; 18lp: 3; 14: 15; 14lc: 1; 16: 2); 17t:141; 17m:67, 394–418; 18:7, 74, 116, 141, 154, 182, 231; 18r:44; 19:29. *Proposed:* keep *spectators*, defined once as the remaining insertions of the correlation.
   *Source:* Scott `part1/02-definitions.tex:216`: "two labels represent the same field when every spectator sees the same answer. The response `ι_d[c]` records those correlations against every spectator list … Write `v(x) = (v_1(x_1), …, v_n(x_n))` for a spectator word"; `:293`: "The product expansion replaces a cluster of nearby fields by fields at one point, inside correlations with distant spectators. … write `S^ζ(A, x; B, y)` for the correlation of the concatenated lists … spectators `y` are `δ_sp`-clear if `|o − y_j| ≥ δ_sp`".
2. **Exterior function.** In `02-equation-section.tex` the bounded measurable function `S` "depending only on links with both endpoints farther than `r_d` from `o`" (2e:39–41).
   *Basis:* R (2e:39–41). *Where:* 2e:195, 205–206, 213, 221, 254. *Proposed:* *the function `S`*; *exterior function*.
   *Source:* Scott `part2/A-section.tex:180`: "An exterior spectator outside `𝔹_r(y)` is a bounded measurable function of the positive links having both endpoints outside `𝔹_r(y)`; it need not be gauge invariant."
*Literature:* name clash. In D2 **spectator variables** are the fields left in holes from earlier stages and no longer integrated (D2 p. 092301-61: "holes which localize spectator variables left over from the early stages of the expansion"), the analogue of v3's frozen links (see *frozen*), not the other insertions of a correlation (sense 1), which have no counterpart. Suggested: keep v3's defined sense, and do not use "spectator" for frozen or conditioning variables.
*Across chapters:* sense 2 only in 2e; sense 1 from chapter 3 to chapter 19. The word is kept rather than replaced by *the remaining insertions* or *auxiliary insertion*: it is used throughout, and "exterior word", "exterior insertions", "external positions" reduce to it.
*See also:* spectator responses.

#### spin operators
- **Meaning.** The linear maps `L_d(K) = c_*^{-1}Y_d(K) : F_d → F_d` (14:837), `K ∈ so(4)`, real-linear in `K`: the part of the infinitesimal rotation that acts on the field components, as opposed to the orbital term `Σ_b (Kx_i)_b ∂_b` of the Ward identity. "This uses no integration of the spin operators into a rotation group" (14:903–904) says that the argument uses only the exponentials `e^{−θL(K)}` of one `K` at a time (14:861), which exist because `F_d` is finite-dimensional, and not a representation of the rotation group. Not defined under this name in v3.

Lean `YM.Ward.SpinRows S := ∀ d : ℕ, Ortho.Skew →ₗ[ℝ] (S.Field d →ₗ[ℂ] S.Field d)`, YM/Ward/Sum.lean (definition read); `YM.Ward.angular`, same file (definition read: `Σ_i (disc(q[i ↦ turns T K (q i)]) x + Σ_b (K x_i)_b · disc(q[i ↦ rise W b (q i)]) x)`, the sum of the spin and orbital terms); `YM.Ward.higher`, YM/Ward/Extreme.lean (statement read: analyticity along a one-coordinate motion, with hypotheses `T : SpinRows S`, `Collinear W T`, `commutes W T`).
*Across chapters:* one occurrence, chapter 14. v3 should name the object at 14:903, as the source sentence does ("finite-dimensional exponentials of individual spin operators").

- **Meaning.** The definition of the Hessian by splitting the field into two factors: it is "obtained from `S(log(e^{x_+}e^{x_-}))` by two `x_+` derivatives" (7:362–363). The increments act by left multiplication, as in the left derivative `D_A^L F(U) = d/dε F(exp(εA_e)U_e)` of 2:318–321.
  *Basis:* R (7:362–363). *Where:* 7:362–363. *Proposed:* *second derivative in left-multiplication increments* (no fixed standard phrase). Not *left-invariant coordinates*: left multiplication is generated by right-invariant vector fields.

#### squarefree source algebra

#### stage
*Variants:* stage `j`; regularity stage; regularity-stage index `J_m`, `J(m)`; stage bound, constant, threshold, requirement, floor, orders; adjacent stage pair; change of stage; fixed-stage tail.
- **Meaning.** "A stage `j ≥ 1` specifies finitely many derivative orders, support exponents, path widths and coefficient bounds" (10:25–26); the stages are nested, and at a fixed stage there are only finitely many permitted adjacent pairs (10:28–31). The stage in force at level `m` is `J(m) = j` for `A_j ≤ m < A_{j+1}` (10:129–134); "`J(m+1)` is the stage used for this step" (10:50); `L_i = 𝓛_{J_i}` with `J_i = J(i+1)` (17w:14–15). It is not a renormalisation step and not a scale: "a regularity-stage index `J_m`; that index is different from the scale `m`" (4:651–652). The uses in chapters 5 and 6, which precede the definition, have this sense: the "adjacent pair of stages" of 5:689 is the pair of stages of the fine and the coarse side of one step, and "Fix a stage" (6:21), "the fixed stage" (6:96) fix this numerical data, on which the constants may depend.
  *Basis:* D (10:25–31; index 10:129–134); S for the uses at 5:689 and 6:21, 96. *Where:* 4:651; 5:689; 6:21, 96; 7:22, 833, 1056, 1067, 1069, 1072, 1203; 9:110, 421, 427, 928, 935; 9s:83, 214; files 10 / 11 / 11R / 11E: 32 / 33 / 7 / 7; ch. 12–16: 23, and 2 idiomatic "at this stage" (14:65; 15:324); ch. 17–19: 23 (17:132; 17w:2, 13, 14, 49, 50, 69, 71, 97, 125; 17c:12, 107, 135, 238; 17m:39, 141, 197, 301, 346, 347, 430; 19:30; RG:34). *Proposed:* keep *stage `j`*, defined once at 10:25 ("A stage `j ≥ 1` specifies finitely many derivative orders, support exponents, path widths and coefficient bounds") and referred to at first use in each chapter, with a forward reference at 5:689 and 6:21; never for a scale or a step.
  *Source:* Lean `YM.RG.Stage`, `YM/RG/History.lean` (definition read): a record of a cutoff profile `clip`, `order ≥ 6`, `power ≥ 2`, `supportExponent`, `width`, `paths`, `drift`, `columns`; `YM.RG.Calendar` in the same file (definition read): `stage : ℕ → Stage`, `J : ℕ → ℕ`, `params m := stage (J m)`, the step `op m p` built with patch order `J (m+1)`, and `Fits.stepSlow : J (m+1) ≤ J m + 1`. For chapter 6: `YM.Pressure.Teller`, `YM/Pressure/Seeds.lean` (definition read) has two stages `top`, `below` and an index `j`, and `Teller.Funds` requires the patch order to equal `j` and the two cutoff profiles to be those of `top` and `below`.
*Literature:* name clash; v3's object (a stage `j`, which specifies finitely many derivative orders, support exponents, path widths and coefficient bounds, 10:25–31) has no counterpart, since `L`, `M` and one set of constants are fixed for all steps (B87 p. 264, Theorem 3; D1 p. 1330010-28). In D2, D3 a **stage** is a step of the iteration (D2 p. 092301-19: "At the kth stage of the iteration we will introduce not one but two new small field regions"; D3 p. 2133: "a sum over the choice of large and small field regions at each stage"). Adopted (23 November 2026): keep *stage `j`*, restricted to `j` and described as the text does at 10:25 ("A stage `j ≥ 1` specifies finitely many derivative orders, support exponents, path widths and coefficient bounds"), never as a "regularity class" or "regularity stage": "regular" is kept for Bałaban's two uses (the regular part of the action; regularity condition, regular configuration). Add a note that in Dimock "stage" means step.
*Across chapters:* one sense throughout. Not *regularity class `j`*, *regularity stage* or *regularity level*, as names or as descriptions: "regular" is kept for the regular part of the action and for the regularity condition, and the third also collides with level `m`. The conditions for entering a stage ("stage entrance") are the lower bounds on the starting scale. "Bottom stage" (17w:97: "imposed at the actual bottom stage … not multiplied once per step") may use the word for a level; not determined. The letter `j` is shared with the smoothing order; in the formalisation the smoothing order of the step `m+1 → m` is the stage index `J(m+1)`, so the two letters denote the same number there.
*See also:* smoothing order; stage plateau; step; schedule.

#### stationary background
*Variants:* background.
- **Meaning.** Used in titles and prose of chapter 5 without a definition; the nearest to a gloss is 5:1286–1287, the action "whose germ at zero defines the background".
  *Basis:* I. *Where:* 5:7, 14, 1222, 1287. *Proposed:* *critical configuration*.
*Literature:* **background field** (B85d p. 277; B85c p. 389, abstract: "These propagators depend on an external gauge field configuration, called a background field"; B85e p. 259; D2 p. 092301-42: "hence on the background field φ⁰_{k+1,Ω}(□*) and the fluctuation field W_k"; BIJ85 p. 308: "expand (3.24) into background and fluctuation parts"). The same object in role; the differences are those stated under *stationary graph*: Bałaban's background field is a `k`-step minimiser under a delta-function constraint, and the effective action is a function of it (B87 (1.3)), whereas v3's is the one-step critical point of action plus penalty. Adopted (23 November 2026): *critical configuration*, the stationary field being the specific configuration determined by the coarse field; this refines the decision of the same day, which had *background field* here. *Background field* is kept for any configuration about which one expands, or at which operators are evaluated or differentiated (Bałaban's "propagators in a background field"; v3 chapter 7), so the critical configuration is called a background field only in that role. The difference from Bałaban's background field is stated at first use (see *stationary graph*): his is a minimum at fixed averages (his "minimal configuration"), v3's a stationary point of fine action plus block penalty for one step.
*Across chapters:* chapter 5; "background insertions" in chapter 17 belong to the entry *background*.
*See also:* stationary graph.

See *stationary graph*.
*Literature:* see *stationary graph*.

#### stationary chart

  *Basis:* R (5:1321–1335). *Where:* 5:1321–1335; 7:867, 1203. *Proposed:* keep *chart* for the neighbourhood; do not use it for the map.

An analogue (existence and uniqueness of the critical point on a neighbourhood). Suggested: keep *chart*; cite B85d Theorem 1 as the counterpart.
*Across chapters:* chapters 5 and 7. Not a name of the critical-configuration map: the chart is the domain, the graph the map (5:1321–1335; 7:867–869).
*See also:* stationary graph; safe chart.
